original_question: Suppose (R, m) is a regular local ring of dimension n and I subset R is an ideal with big height e. Do the following containments hold: (1) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r) I^r for m >= rn; (2) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r-(n-1)) I^r for m >= rn - (n - 1); (3) I^(m) subset m^(re-r) I^r for m >= re; and (4) I^(m) subset m^(re-r-(e-1)) I^r for m >= re - (e - 1)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.8, Problem 2.8.2 (the Harbourne–Huneke four-part local containment problem for symbolic powers).
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct local setup from the paper: a regular local ring, its maximal ideal, the dimension n, an ideal I of big height e, and the same four candidate containments with the right exponents on the maximal-ideal factor and on I^r. It also correctly captures that the question is not the usual containment I^(m) ⊆ I^r, but a sharpened version with an extra power of the maximal ideal on the right.
missing_details: The exact target in the paper is Problem 2.8.2 in Section 2.8, not the preceding Conjecture 2.8.1.
The paper asks the question uniformly for all positive integers r and all symbolic exponents satisfying the displayed lower bounds; those quantifiers should be stated explicitly.
To make the question stand-alone, the symbolic-power notation should be defined, since Problem 2.8.2 concerns an arbitrary ideal in a local ring, not only a radical ideal on a variety.
The big height should be defined explicitly as bight(I) = max{ht P : P is a minimal prime of I}.
The notation should distinguish the maximal ideal \mathfrak m from the symbolic-power index; your draft uses m for both.
Paper-faithfully, the displayed thresholds in Problem 2.8.2 are written with strict inequalities: m > rn, m > rn-(n-1), m > re, and m > re-(e-1), rather than with \u2265 at the same bound.

No homogeneity, grading, projective-space, or field hypothesis belongs in the formal statement of Problem 2.8.2; the motivating discussion in Section 2.8 begins on a smooth complex variety, but the problem itself is purely local and ring-theoretic.
It should be clear that \mathfrak m^a I^r means the product of the ordinary a-th power of the maximal ideal with the ordinary r-th power of I.
The paper phrases this as four separate subquestions ('Then do the following hold?'), so the refined version should preserve that four-part structure inside one research question.
refined_question: Let (R, \mathfrak m) be a regular local ring of Krull dimension n, let I \subseteq R be an arbitrary ideal of big height e := \operatorname{bight}(I) = \max\{\operatorname{ht} P : P is a minimal prime of I\}, and for each integer s \ge 1 let I^{(s)} := \bigcap_{P \in \operatorname{Ass}(R/I)} (I^s R_P \cap R) denote the s-th symbolic power of I. Is it true that for every integer r \ge 1, the following four uniform containments hold whenever the indicated lower bound on s is satisfied: (1) I^{(s)} \subseteq \mathfrak m^{rn-r} I^r for all s > rn; (2) I^{(s)} \subseteq \mathfrak m^{rn-r-(n-1)} I^r for all s > rn-(n-1); (3) I^{(s)} \subseteq \mathfrak m^{re-r} I^r for all s > re; and (4) I^{(s)} \subseteq \mathfrak m^{re-r-(e-1)} I^r for all s > re-(e-1)?
justification: The draft is trying to restate Problem 2.8.2 exactly. In Section 2.8 the paper first recalls symbolic powers, the Ein–Lazarsfeld–Smith/Hochster–Huneke containment I^(re) \subseteq I^r, and the definition of big height; it then states Harbourne's Conjecture 2.8.1 about improving the left-hand exponent. Immediately after that, the paper says that Harbourne–Huneke ask whether one can instead improve the right-hand side by inserting powers of the maximal ideal, and it formulates precisely the same four containments appearing in your draft. Section 3.12 explicitly refers back to these as 'the improved versions in Problem 2.8.2,' confirming that this is the precise target and not a broader neighboring conjecture.
